headline: Town's overdue audits and $10 million state aid plan were discussed; new Finance Director starts December 4.
summary: Interim Finance Director Myron Hul said the Town will miss the December 31, 2026 audit deadline. He estimated about a 50% chance of finishing the fiscal 2026 closeout by the end of November. The commission also approved the minutes of its October 1, 2026 meeting.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 1, 2026 meeting by a 4-0 roll call vote.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Finance Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
6:00 PM, November 12, 2026 
 
 
 
Memorial Town Hall 
2372 Whitney Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL 
  
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner R. Scolnic at 6:03 PM. 
 
The Clerk called the roll, and the following members were: 
 
Present: 
Commissioner Rabbi Benjamin Scolnic, Chair 
Commissioner Michael Martin 
Commissioner Thomas Fortuna 
Commissioner Arnold Margolis 
 
Absent: 
Commissioner Myles Carter-Solomon, Youth 
Commissioner Bethany McCluster 
 
Also in attendance were Director of Finance Myron Hul; Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards 
and Commissions Clerk, in person; Dr. Mario Ciccarini, Hamden Board of Education 
Member; Commissioner Thomas Fortuna; Commissioner Arnold Margolis; and 4 members 
of the public joining virtually. 
2. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 Chairman R. Scolnic requested a motion to adopt the minutes from Thursday, October 1st, 
2026. 
 
The motion was made by T. Fortuna and seconded by Commissioner M. Martin. 
 
Vote by Roll Call: 
 
Yes 
Commissioner R. Scolnic, Chair  
Commissioner M. Martin 
Commissioner T. Fortuna 
Commissioner A. Margolis 
 
No
Absent 
Commissioner B. McCluster 
Commissioner M. Carter-Solomon, Youth 
 
The motion passed. 
 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 4, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 2 
 
3. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION 
  
 No public comment was offered. 
4. REPORT FROM EX-OFFICIO MEMBERS 
  
 
 
  1. Public Official or municipal employee representing the Mayor, designated by the  
Mayor  
  Interim Finance Director Myron W. Hul updated the Commission on the Town's 
financial position, outstanding municipal audits, the appointment of a permanent 
Finance Director, and the five-year financial plan submitted to the Connecticut Office 
of Policy and Management (OPM). 
 
Appointment of New Finance Director 
 
The Commission discussed Mayor Adam Sendroff's November 3, 2026 
announcement appointing Dawn V. Savo as Hamden's new Finance Director. Ms. D. 
Savo is scheduled to begin her position on December 4, 2026. Mr. Hul reported that 
he expects to remain available for several weeks to assist with the transition and 
ensure continuity within the Finance Department. Commissioners expressed optimism 
regarding the appointment and the opportunity to strengthen the Town's financial 
operations. 
 
Outstanding Municipal Audits 
 
Interim Director M. Hul reported that the Finance Department continued working with 
its external auditors, CBIZ, and financial consultants, CliftonLarsonAllen (CLA), to 
resolve outstanding audit issues. At the request of CBIZ, the Town reopened its 
review of fiscal year 2023 financial records to substantiate ending balances before 
proceeding with the fiscal year 2024 audit. 
 
Interim Director M. Hul identified four principal areas requiring additional reconciliation 
or supporting documentation: 
 
1. Cash and Bank Reconciliations: Most bank accounts had been reconciled, with a 
small number of accounts requiring further review. The Deputy Finance Director 
reviewed the Documentation and provided it to CLA for independent evaluation.
2. Fixed Assets and Depreciation: The Town was reviewing approximately $10 million 
in fixed-asset depreciation calculations and supporting documentation with its former 
external auditor, Clermont. The Town recently received additional information and was 
evaluating it. 
 
3. Board of Education Financial Accounts: Differences remained between the Board of 
Education's reported accounts payable, payroll, and receivable balances and amounts 
reflected in previously published financial statements. A follow-up meeting with Board 
of Education financial staff was scheduled to reconcile the discrepancies. 
 
4. Pension Investments and Cash: The Finance Department was examining 
approximately $2.3 million in pension-related expenditures recorded near the end of 
fiscal year 2023. Mr. Hul explained that the timing of pension payments around the 
June 30 fiscal year-end and July 1 payment date could account for differences 
between the supporting records and financial statements. An additional discrepancy of 
approximately $500,000 was also under review with the Town's pension specialist and 
third-party investment administrator. 
 
Mr. Hul explained that once these issues were resolved, CBIZ would determine 
whether any remaining discrepancies were material to the financial statements. 
 
If the auditors accepted the fiscal year 2023 ending balances, the Town could resume 
the fiscal year 2024 audit using those amounts as the opening balances. 
 
He stated that substantial fiscal year 2024 documentation had already been provided, 
but the review was temporarily suspended while the fiscal year 2023 balances were 
being examined. 
 
Commissioners expressed concern about the length of time required to complete the 
audits and emphasized the importance of resolving the outstanding issues before 
additional fiscal years became delinquent. 
 
Fiscal Year 2026 Closeout and Audit Deadlines 
 
Mr. Hul reported that fiscal year 2026 ended on June 30, 2026, but the Town had not 
yet completed its year-end financial closeout. 
 
The original target date of approximately October 15 had passed, and the Finance 
Department was working toward completing the closeout by the end of November. 
 
Mr. Hul stated that he considered the likelihood of meeting the revised deadline 
approximately 50%. 
 
He acknowledged that the Town would not meet the December 31, 2026 statutory 
audit deadline. 
 
Mr. Hul explained that the Finance Department needed to establish stronger year-end 
closing procedures, identify operational bottlenecks, and improve internal processes 
to ensure future financial reporting deadlines could be met.
He noted that municipalities that miss statutory audit deadlines must continue 
reporting their delinquent status to OPM. 
 
Five-Year Financial Plan and Municipal Finance Advisory Commission 
 
Mr. Hul reported that the Town had prepared a five-year financial plan in connection 
with state legislation and Hamden's participation in Tier I financial oversight. 
 
The plan had been provided to OPM and the Municipal Finance Advisory Commission 
(MFAC) for review. 
 
OPM had provided feedback, and the Finance Department was incorporating 
applicable recommendations into the revised document. 
 
Mr. Hul explained that the plan remained a working document between the Town 
administration and OPM and would become publicly available upon its formal 
submission and publication with the MFAC meeting materials. 
 
The Town was scheduled to present its financial plan to MFAC on Wednesday, 
November 18, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. 
 
The scheduled presentation would address Hamden's fiscal recovery efforts, 
outstanding audits, financial planning, and eligibility for state financial assistance. 
 
Mayor Adam Sendroff, Interim Finance Director Myron W. Hul, Deputy Finance 
Director Rick Galarza, and Superintendent Gary Highsmith were identified among the 
Town officials scheduled to participate. 
 
Mr. Hul explained that approval or acceptance of the five-year financial plan would 
help determine the amount of financial assistance available to Hamden under 
legislation authorizing up to $10 million in state support. 
 
Commissioners discussed the potential use of the funding and its effect on the Town's 
financial position. 
 
Mr. Hul reported that, if Hamden received the full $10 million, the Mayor's proposed 
allocation would be approximately: 
- $5 million to strengthen the Town's fund balance. 
- $5 million for urgently needed municipal infrastructure improvements, including 
heating and cooling systems, building repairs, and roadway improvements. 
Mr. Hul emphasized the Mayor's position that one-time revenue should not be used to 
support recurring operating expenditures. 
 
Commissioners discussed whether some funding could be directed toward improving 
the Finance Department's operational capacity. Mr. Hul reiterated the administration's 
preference to avoid creating recurring financial obligations using nonrecurring 
revenue. 
 
The Commission also discussed the Town's financial reserves and the requirements
for restoring access to the municipal bond market. 
 
Mr. Hul explained that the Town's fund balance ordinance establishes a target of 
approximately 7% of annual operating expenditures, equivalent to approximately $21 
million. 
 
He noted that commonly recommended reserve levels are higher, approximately 15–
20% of operating expenditures. 
 
Mr. Hul emphasized that completing the outstanding audits would be a critical step 
toward restoring relationships with bond-rating agencies and regaining access to the 
municipal bond market. 
 
He cautioned that the completion of the audits would not immediately restore the 
Town's bond rating, as additional review and evaluation would be required. 
 
Current Financial Position and Tax Collections 
 
Commissioners requested an update on the Town's current fund balance and cash 
position. 
 
Mr. Hul stated that the Town's estimated fund balance at the end of the previous fiscal 
year was slightly below $10 million, although he emphasized that the figure was 
preliminary and subject to reconciliation and audit. 
 
He reported that the Town generally budgets for a property-tax collection rate of 
approximately 98%. 
 
Mr. Hul stated that he was not aware of significant deviations from anticipated tax 
collections. 
 
He also distinguished between the Town's available operating cash and its fund 
balance, explaining that the two measures serve different financial purposes. 
 
Although the Finance Department did not currently produce a formal treasury report, 
Mr. Hul stated that discussions with the Deputy Finance Director indicated that the 
Town maintained sufficient cash to support its day-to-day operations. 
 
Finance Department Organizational and Staffing Review 
 
Mr. Hul reported that CLA was conducting an organizational assessment of the 
Finance Department and related municipal financial operations. 
 
The assessment began in approximately mid-October 2026 and was expected to be 
completed by mid-January 2027. 
 
CLA had conducted initial interviews with employees in Finance, Procurement, 
Assessment, and Tax Collection. 
 
The consultants were also reviewing organizational charts, job descriptions, collective
bargaining agreements, and other relevant departmental information. 
 
Commissioners asked whether the review would include recommendations for 
additional positions or changes to the Finance Department's organizational structure. 
 
Mr. Hul explained that he preferred to allow the consultants to independently evaluate 
the department's needs. 
 
He noted that the possibility of establishing an internal audit function had been 
discussed as a potential area for consideration, but no formal recommendation had 
been made. 
 
Commissioners emphasized the importance of using the assessment to strengthen 
internal controls, improve efficiency, and establish sustainable financial management 
procedures. 
 
Legislative Financial Commentary 
 
A commissioner asked about financial commentary and a series of online videos 
published by State Representative Josh Elliott concerning Hamden's finances. 
 
Mr. Hul stated that he had not recently communicated with Representative Elliott and 
was not familiar with the specific videos. 
 
The Commission reported that Representative Elliott had been invited to attend the 
next meeting to discuss his findings and observations. 
  2. Representative of the Board of Education, designated by a majority vote of said 
Board  
  Dr. Mario Ciccarini, a member of the Hamden Board of Education, provided an update 
following the Board's recent Finance Subcommittee and regular Board meetings. Dr. 
M. Ciccarini reported that the Board of Education's overall budget remained on track, 
except for special education expenditures, which exceeded anticipated spending 
levels. He explained that the expected expenditure rate at this point in the fiscal year 
was approximately 25%, while several special education budget line items had 
reached between 33% and 40%. 
 
Dr. M. Ciccarini attributed the increased expenditures to a combination of students 
entering the district with existing Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and 
students already enrolled in Hamden schools who required additional services or 
alternative educational placements. He reported that approximately 145 students with 
existing IEPs had entered the district during the current school year. He noted that 
even a relatively small number of students requiring intensive services could 
significantly affect the special education budget. 
 
Dr. M. Ciccarini explained that special education eligibility encompasses 11 disability 
categories. He identified autism spectrum disorder, specific learning disabilities such 
as dyslexia, and other health impairments (OHI), including attention-
deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), as among the most common categories. He also 
discussed students with speech and language impairments, developmental delays,
and significant medical needs. Some medically fragile students require specialized 
transportation and medical support during the school day, which can result in 
additional costs. 
 
Dr. M. Ciccarini explained that preschool-aged children may be identified as having 
developmental delays before a more specific disability classification is established. He 
also clarified that when medication must be administered at school, parents or 
guardians must provide properly labeled medication and the required authorization. 
Dr. M. Ciccarini stated that the Board of Education's business office had been 
communicating with the Mayor's Office regarding the expenditure increases to ensure 
that the Town remained informed of potential budgetary impacts. He further reported 
that preparation of the next fiscal year's education budget was beginning. The Board 
of Education anticipated reviewing the proposed budget in January and February 
2027 before submitting its formal request to the Mayor's Office. 
 
Commissioners asked about enrollment trends and whether the district had 
experienced significant population changes. 
 
Dr. M. Ciccarini stated that available state data indicated that Hamden's overall 
student enrollment had remained relatively stable over the preceding decade, with 
some annual increases and decreases. He did not have the total number of students 
entering or leaving the district during the current school year. 
 
The Commission thanked Dr. M. Ciccarini for his report. 
  3. Chair of the Legislative Council committee of jurisdiction over the budget or a 
member  
of said committee designated by the Chair  
  
 
5. UPDATE REPORT FROM THE FINANCE COMMISSION CHAIR 
  
 
 
 1. Pension Obligations 
       
  Commissioner T. Fortuna requested an update regarding the Commission's previous 
discussions concerning municipal pension obligations. 
 
Chairman R. Scolnic reported that several individuals met with a representative of a 
nonprofit organization familiar with pension funding strategies used by other 
municipalities. 
 
The representative had discussed potential approaches to addressing pension 
liabilities and long-term funding challenges. 
 
Chairman R. Scolnic stated that he had attempted to facilitate a meeting between the 
representative and Mayor A. Sendroff; however, to his knowledge, a follow-up 
meeting had not yet occurred. 
 
No additional developments were available to report.
6. UPDATE REPORT FROM THE MUNICIPAL BOARD AND COMMISSIONS, INVITED 
GUEST 
  
 The Commission's discussion with Interim Finance Director M. Hul included the Town's 
outstanding financial audits, the five-year financial plan, the upcoming MFAC presentation, 
the Finance Department organizational review, and financial recovery priorities, as 
documented above. 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No executive session was held. 
8. REGULAR AGENDA 
  
 No additional matters were brought forward under the regular agenda. 
9. UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
  
 No additional unfinished business was discussed. 
10. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 No new business was introduced. 
11. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 Commissioner A. Margolis moved to adjourn the meeting, and Commissioner T. Fortuna 
seconded. 
 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
The Finance Commission adjourned the meeting at approximately 6:38 PM.
